evidences.report_id: Cylance SPEAR Team_ A Threat Actor Resurfaces
evidences.text: Several months ago I examined a malware-tainted Word document titled “ISIS_twitter_list.doc.” I didn’t think much of it and quickly moved on after a cursory analysis.

evidences.report_id: Cylance SPEAR Team_ A Threat Actor Resurfaces
evidences.text: Name ISIS_twitter_list.doc File Size 146,338 bytes The first stage shellcode searches for the marker "GfCv" then checks the next four bytes are "EF FE EC CE" in the document then decodes the second stage shellcode using the four-byte XOR key "0x29F7C592".

evidences.report_id: Cylance SPEAR Team_ A Threat Actor Resurfaces
evidences.text: The decoded binary will be written to the filesystem as " %APPDATA%\Microsoft\Systemcertificates\Certificates.ocx ".

evidences.report_id: Cylance SPEAR Team_ A Threat Actor Resurfaces
evidences.text: Registry Persistence Key HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run\Certificates Registry Key Value Rundll32.exe "%APPDATA%\Microsoft\SystemCertificates\Certificates.ocx",Setup

evidences.report_id: Cylance SPEAR Team_ A Threat Actor Resurfaces
evidences.text: The binary is configured to communicate to "www.microsoftservices.proxydns.com" on port 80 using standard HTTP POST and GET requests.

evidences.report_id: Cylance SPEAR Team_ A Threat Actor Resurfaces
evidences.text: Additionally the dynamic DNS domains "fighthard.mooo.com" and "rampage.freetcp.com" have both historically resolved to this IP address.

evidences.report_id: Cylance SPEAR Team_ A Threat Actor Resurfaces
evidences.text: Several additional exploit documents were identified by investigating the domains "fighthard.mooo.com" and "rampage.freetcp.com".

evidences.report_id: Cylance SPEAR Team_ A Threat Actor Resurfaces
evidences.text: Down the Intelligence Rabbit Hole Fighthard.mooo.com additionally resolved to 173.224.214.12 in February of 2014.

evidences.report_id: Cylance SPEAR Team_ A Threat Actor Resurfaces
evidences.text: Rampage.freetcp.com still resolves to 103.229.125.157 as of 4/2/2015 Let's go ahead and take a look further into one of the other expoit documents, name=CVE-2012-0158) , but instead of using a MIME encoded document this file was just a plain RTX document.

evidences.report_id: Cylance SPEAR Team_ A Threat Actor Resurfaces
evidences.text: Upon successful exploitation the decoded binary will be written first to %TEMP%\dw20.EXE then copied to

evidences.report_id: Cylance SPEAR Team_ A Threat Actor Resurfaces
evidences.text: On reboot explorer.exe was now happy to load the backdoor and get down to business; this technique is known as dll search order hijacking or binary planting.

evidences.report_id: Cylance SPEAR Team_ A Threat Actor Resurfaces
evidences.text: The backdoor contains identical exports as well as an additional dummy function from the legitimate msacm32.drv called "StartWork" which can be used to reliably identify similar samples.

evidences.report_id: Cylance SPEAR Team_ A Threat Actor Resurfaces
evidences.text: The backdoor interestingly contains the well known Poison Ivy RAT shellcode as well as its own custom backdoor.

evidences.report_id: Cylance SPEAR Team_ A Threat Actor Resurfaces
evidences.text: It will first attempt to communicate to fighthard.mooo.com using the poison ivy binary protocol with the default connection password of "admin".

evidences.report_id: Cylance SPEAR Team_ A Threat Actor Resurfaces
evidences.text: The Poison Ivy shellcode is encrypted using a custom cipher with the key "Tiger324{" beginning at offset 0xFA5 and ending at 0x159E.

evidences.report_id: Cylance SPEAR Team_ A Threat Actor Resurfaces
evidences.text: If this initial connection fails it will revert to the secondary backdoor, which utilizes HTTP GET and POST requests somewhat similar to the ones described above to the internal IP address "192.168.2.26".

evidences.report_id: Cylance SPEAR Team_ A Threat Actor Resurfaces
evidences.text: Host: 192.168.2.26 Requests may also be made to the following pages: "check.asp", "result.asp", and "upload.asp".

evidences.report_id: Cylance SPEAR Team_ A Threat Actor Resurfaces
evidences.text: XEJ7OZkvwBZVx1JsrhQ==' unb64 = base64.b64decode(req,'+*') print dec The request decodes to "123|000000+|USER-D6921F6215|Administrator|-1676096002|1.0|0|", where values are separated by the delimiter "|".

evidences.report_id: Cylance SPEAR Team_ A Threat Actor Resurfaces
evidences.text: "USER-D6921F6215" is the hostname of the victim, "Administrator" is the victim user, "1676096002" is the current Date/Time in decimal, and "1.0" is a version number also stored in the backdoor.The 16-byte XOR key will be randomly generated per each request.

evidences.report_id: Cylance SPEAR Team_ A Threat Actor Resurfaces
evidences.text: The "173.224.214.12" IP address that "fighthard.mooo.com" previously resolved to also historically had two other domains point to it "queenberry.www1.biz" and "word.crabdance.com".

evidences.report_id: Cylance SPEAR Team_ A Threat Actor Resurfaces
